sigma_definition.note: spec 02 §4.9 names poly2/R=12; this build's frozen convention is the pipeline's (D-007/D-008). Findings under a different convention are not comparable.
sigma_definition.change_policy: any change bumps registry_version and invalidates all stored Findings

hypotheses.title: Comigration of the R-lane band with the standard
hypotheses.plain_language: A band in the reaction lane sits at the same position as the standard. Comigration is consistent with identity; it is never identity.
hypotheses.falsifier: Running the same pair in a second, orthogonal solvent system, or as a co-spot (H02), would separate them if they are different.

hypotheses.title: The co-spot test
hypotheses.plain_language: When the reaction mixture and the standard are spotted on top of each other, two resolved bands are a positive result — the materials differ; one band only says they were not distinguished here.
hypotheses.falsifier: If the two-band appearance is an artefact of overloading, halving the co-lane load will collapse it to one band.

hypotheses.title: Band inventory of the R lane at the reporting gate
hypotheses.plain_language: How many bands the reaction lane shows at 5 sigma with ensemble agreement, next to what blank plates yield at the same gate.
hypotheses.falsifier: A blank lane on the same plate at the same gate must show zero bands; if it does not, the count is a noise artefact.

hypotheses.title: Origin residue present
hypotheses.plain_language: Material remains at the application point: either very polar material or simple overload. One plate cannot tell these apart.
hypotheses.falsifier: Spot the same sample at half the load; residue that shrinks in proportion was overload.

hypotheses.title: Streak / tailing: not quantifiable
hypotheses.plain_language: A streaking lane has no discrete band position or area. Readings: overload; an acidic/basic compound on unbuffered silica; decomposition on the plate.
hypotheses.falsifier: Re-run at lower load, or with 1% acetic acid in the eluent; a streak that resolves was overload or acidity.

hypotheses.title: Lane-role consistency
hypotheses.plain_language: The lane count and labels come from the operator, never from the signal; the grid is forced to the declared count.
hypotheses.falsifier: An operator-declared lane count that disagrees with the visible lanes is a data-entry problem, not a measurement.

hypotheses.title: Absence of the starting material in the R lane (bounded)
hypotheses.plain_language: If starting material were present above the stated limit at the S-lane position it would have been seen. This is a limit statement, never 'reaction complete'.
hypotheses.falsifier: A single HPLC or NMR point on the same aliquot bounds the residual starting material independently.

hypotheses.title: A new band above the product Rst
hypotheses.plain_language: A band higher than the product that is absent from the S and sd lanes: over-reaction, oxidation, or an eluent-borne artefact.
hypotheses.falsifier: Re-spot from a fresh aliquot with fresh eluent; an eluent artefact disappears, a product does not.

hypotheses.title: Rst of the R-lane principal band
hypotheses.plain_language: The identity coordinate a chemist copies into the notebook, with its ensemble interval. Always Rst, never Rf.
hypotheses.falsifier: Re-develop in a freshly equilibrated chamber; Rst that moves was chamber or solvent, not compound.

hypotheses.title: Co-spot elongation ratio
hypotheses.plain_language: Width of the co-lane band relative to its components; broadening above 1.30 suggests partial resolution.
hypotheses.falsifier: A longer development or an orthogonal solvent system resolves a genuinely broadened co-spot into two bands.

hypotheses.title: Starting-material consumption across a time series
hypotheses.plain_language: The starting-material band in the reaction lane should fade as the reaction proceeds.
hypotheses.needs: 6 plates in one campaign, one solvent system, constant loading, no clipping
hypotheses.falsifier: If loading was not constant, the same decline appears with no chemistry. Re-spot the archived aliquots at equal load on one plate.

hypotheses.title: Product appearance / growth
hypotheses.plain_language: The product band should darken as the reaction proceeds.
hypotheses.needs: 6 plates in one campaign, one solvent system, constant loading, no clipping; product absent from the S lane on every plate
hypotheses.falsifier: Re-spot archived aliquots at equal load on one plate; a loading artefact does not reproduce.

hypotheses.title: Starting material and product are anti-correlated across a time series
hypotheses.plain_language: As the reaction proceeds, the starting-material spot should fade as the product spot darkens.
hypotheses.needs: 6 plates in one campaign, one solvent system, constant loading, no clipping, both bands in the linear OD range
hypotheses.falsifier: If the loading was not held constant, the same pattern appears with no chemistry. Re-spot archived aliquots at equal load on one plate.

hypotheses.title: Impurity-count trend across a series
hypotheses.plain_language: Whether the number of side bands changes across the series, after removing the phantom baseline.
hypotheses.needs: 8 plates in one campaign and a passing synthetic-blank cohort control
hypotheses.falsifier: If band count truly tracked reaction progress, it would still do so after conditioning on image noise.

hypotheses.title: Conversion proxy from area ratio (trend)
hypotheses.plain_language: area(product)/[area(product)+area(SM)] within one lane; equals conversion only if both compounds absorb equally at 254 nm.
hypotheses.needs: 6 plates in one campaign; no clipping on either band; both peaks in OD 0.05–1.0; epsilon_comparable declared yes
hypotheses.falsifier: Quantitative TLC densitometry is ±10–20% at best; a single HPLC or NMR point on the same aliquot calibrates or falsifies it.

hypotheses.title: Rst drift across a plate series (negative control on the chemistry)
hypotheses.plain_language: If the R-lane principal band's Rst moves by more than 0.05 across plates, the chromatography changed and identity claims across those plates are void.
hypotheses.needs: 3 plates with an sd lane and an R lane
hypotheses.falsifier: Re-develop two archived plates side by side in a freshly equilibrated chamber; if Rst realigns, it was the chamber.

hypotheses.title: Band position must not move with reaction time
hypotheses.plain_language: A compound's Rst does not depend on how long the flask was stirred; a position that moves is an artefact or two co-eluting species.
hypotheses.falsifier: A position that moves with time but not with chamber re-equilibration indicates co-eluting species; a second solvent system separates them.

hypotheses.title: Origin residue vs lane load
hypotheses.plain_language: Residue fraction that rises with load is overload; residue independent of load is a polar decomposition product.
hypotheses.needs: 1 plate with a ≥3-point loading series of the same sample
hypotheses.falsifier: A loading series whose residue fraction is flat across loads refutes the overload reading.

hypotheses.title: Tailing vs lane load
hypotheses.plain_language: Tailing that grows with load confirms H05's overload reading.
hypotheses.needs: 1 plate with a ≥3-point loading series of the same sample
hypotheses.falsifier: Tailing that is present at the lowest load is not overload.

hypotheses.title: Impurity count by campaign
hypotheses.plain_language: Does one route or batch consistently give more bands?
hypotheses.falsifier: Within-campaign spread larger than between-campaign differences refutes a campaign effect.

hypotheses.title: Endpoint time by campaign
hypotheses.plain_language: When each campaign reached its endpoint.
hypotheses.needs: 6 campaigns with a resolved endpoint each
hypotheses.falsifier: An endpoint that shifts with capture exposure rather than time is a detection artefact.

hypotheses.title: System-suitability drift (QC chart)
hypotheses.plain_language: The sd band's apparent position and width over calendar time, charted without a p-value from plate 2 onward.
hypotheses.falsifier: A drift that follows chamber changes rather than dates is chamber, not plate lot.
